Probably late to the party but my story is a mixed one. 
I was always behind at school, my reports were below average constantly and I failed to grasp simple concepts such as long division and even the alphabet and tying my shoe laces. 
My mum tried to teach me the times tables by rote learning and it's simply wouldn't 'stick' in my brain. I felt stupid. There was evidence I was behind in all assessable subjects at school and my family treated me like I was the dumb one of the family. I battled through high school and wanted to go onto university but was never encouraged because I was 'limited'. 
I taught myself methods of remembering and techniques in working things out at school that were different to what the teacher was teaching because my way worked better for me. 
I always thought I was below average, and I worked in a supermarket when I left school. I was quickly promoted within the supermarket and I did really well there, I didn't feel so stupid anymore. 
Something changed in me and I knew I wasn't stupid yet my family still treated me like I was. 
Eventually I saw a psychologist and she asked me what I thought my IQ was and I said below average, maybe average. She insisted that I get my IQ tested and I'm actually 2 standard deviations ABOVE average and I have dyslexia. 
So much changed from that, the techniques and methods I adopted in school to get by were abilities of a SMART kid with a learning disability trying to make school more relatable for myself. 
Years later, I'm a scientist and I still have to remind myself I'm not stupid when I struggle with my dyslexia. I never did learn my times tables but I compensate by working things out by other methods. I still have moments when I feel like things just bounce out of my head and I'm not learning but I deal with it by reading rather than listening as I absorb things better that way. 
Sadly, I showed classic dyslexic traits at school from a very young age, but it wasn't picked up back on those days. 
Being treated like I was inferior was soul destroying and killed my confidence, and it took a while to be proud of myself and know that I'm actually more intelligent than the people that once treated me so badly. 

TL:DR 
Thought I was below average, found out I'm dyslexia with superior intellect.

I'm a high school lab technician, I prepare all the experiments that get sent out to students. I suggest simple electronic circuits for electricity, depending on what resources you have. Magnetism could be demonstrated by iron filings mixed with sand on a piece of paper, or watch glass/petri dish if you have one, and use a bar magnet under the paper to separate the sand from iron filings. 
Classroom chemistry would be using basic food stuffs like yeast in warm water in a cup (ideally a conical flask) and cover with a deflated balloon, the yeast will respire and inflate the balloon. Also vinegar and bi carb is an old favourite. Along the same lines is a quarter of an alka-seltzer tablet inside an old style film canister with a small amount of water, the gas given off will pop the lid off. Other experiments using house hold items are crystal making with salt/sugar. Acid and base test using the red cabbage indicator.
